Hi everyone! Since the field is moving too fast and the evidence and discussion are scattered across multiple sites, I recently built a website around open mathematical problems claimed to have been solved or advanced using AI: https://aimath.robertj1.com and will update it everyday!

Several members of the community have already helped improve it. In particular, @Jason Rute suggested the more cautious “claimed to be solved” framing and encouraged tracking precisely what Lean verifies including incorrect statements or formalizations that later fail instead of treating “Lean” as a blanket verification label:)! I’d really appreciate any corrections, missing cases, or further feature suggestions!

Very cool website :)
I think some visual statistics (like graph of when the proofs where published) would be nice.
It is great that you included "research activity"; it would be cool to be able to sort by that as well.
Thank you! I just updated the site to have those features!
I think that a AI generated tractability estimate, could help people decide if attempt something.
Is there a possibility to suggest preprints?
Sure, i can try my best to update it to include those preprints!

FWIW https://mathstodon.xyz/@Jose_A_Alonso/116991853464844319
Strange that both were created 12 hours apart
Oh wow i did not even know that: ) but seems cool! ty!
